title: Operator workpad — API degradation tactics and quick triage
content:
Purpose:
This is a fast operator workpad for investigating and mitigating common API degradations: client-facing timeouts, 429 bursts, streaming stalls (partial responses or paused chunks), and elevated 5xx/error rates.

Scope / audience:
- Primary: on-call SRE and runtime engineers.
- Secondary: platform and serving-runtime devs for follow-ups.
- Not for customer-facing postmortem (this is internal triage content).

Design principles (working assumptions):
- Keep customers serving: graceful degradation, fallback to cheaper model variants, short-term circuit breakers.
- Preserve observability context: preserve traces, avoid dropping logs unless storage is saturated.
- Prefer targeted mitigations over broad rollbacks when possible.

Key signals to check first (5-minute triage):
1) Spike in 429s: check rate limiter saturation + upstream capacity.
   - Dashboards: API -> per-route 429 rate / minute.
   - Quick query: prometheus: sum(rate(api_responses_total{code="429"}[2m])) by (route)
2) Latency/timeouts: p95/p99 increase, queue time growth, worker saturation.
   - prometheus: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le,route))
3) Streaming stalls: client connections open but no tokens forwarded, gap in stream heartbeats.
   - Check edge proxy (nginx/envoy) active downstream connections + last downstream write time.
   - Logs: look for repeated "client reset" or "write timeout" in proxy logs.
4) Elevated 5xx / error rate: look for a leading component (model-serving, router, infra).
   - prometheus: sum(rate(api_responses_total{code=~"5.."}[2m])) by (component)
content_addendum:
Quick triage checklist (ordered):
- Validate the alert: time window, affected routes, customer impact scope.
- Isolate blast radius: are only a subset of routes degraded? specific region? Dedicated vs hosted?
- Identify upstream (model) vs downstream (client) vs infra (gpupool, k8s nodes, db).
- Temporary mitigation: enable per-customer rate limiting, reduce max tokens, disable streaming for heavy routes.

Immediate mitigation recipes:
A) 429 surge:
  - Cause: burst traffic or rate-limiter misconfiguration or licensing/backpressure from downstream.
  - Actions:
    1) Short-term: raise soft rate-limiter quota by X% for affected tier (config store toggle), or enable burst allowance window.
       - Where: feature toggles -> /config/ratelimit -> set route override.
    2) If rate limiter healthy but backend saturated: redirect traffic to a lower-cost model variant (policy: route -> fallback-model = model-small-v2).
       - Command: curl -X POST ${CONTROL_PLANE_API}/routes/override -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","fallback":"model-small-v2","ttl":300}'
    3) Engage client-tier throttling: add 429-based Retry-After headers and short backoff hints.
  - Notes: raising limits increases token spend; coordinate with oncall lead.

B) Timeouts / high latency:
  - Cause: kernel saturation, queueing in inference runtime, poor batching, or inter-region cross-talk.
  - Actions:
    1) Check node CPU/GPU utilization: kubectl top pods -n inference | sort -r -k3
    2) Inspect per-request seq-length distribution (long prompts cause high tail latency). If tail driven, temporarily reject requests above token threshold at edge.
    3) If queue backlog visible: enable emergency autoscale (scale-group: inference-pool -> +X nodes) via infra console or k8s HPA override.
    4) If kernel/driver thrash suspected: restart affected pod(s) with graceful drain, one at a time. kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime --namespace inference --field-selector metadata.name=runtime-abc
  - Fast fallback: reduce batching window to lower p99 at cost of throughput (control-plane -> batching.policy -> latency-mode).

C) Streaming stalls / partial streams:
  - Cause: connection proxy hiccup, model backend stuck producing, kv-cache contention.
  - Actions:
    1) Check proxy logs (envoy/nginx): grep for "upstream timed out" or "downstream reset" in last 15m.
    2) If many connections in ESTABLISHED but no bytes in 30s, restart edge-proxy pod.
    3) If backend stuck: identify request id in trace and attach to model runtime logs; consider killing the specific worker handling that request to free KV cache.
    4) As a temporary customer-impact reduction, switch heavy streaming routes to non-streaming chunked responses (wrap response and stream in smaller atomic messages).

D) Elevated 5xx / runtime errors:
  - Cause: model OOM, null pointer in new release, dependency outage.
  - Actions:
    1) Correlate deploy events: check recent rollouts in last 30m (kubectl get rs --namespace inference --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp).
    2) If rollout suspected: rollback to last stable revision quickly, or scale down new revision to zero. kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime --namespace inference
    3) If OOMs: examine pod OOMKilled events (kubectl describe pod). Consider reducing model size or pinning quantized variant.
    4) If external dependency (vector DB / KMS) is failing: apply degraded mode that returns cached embeddings or masked KV access.

Operational commands cheat-sheet (common snippets):
- Check tail errors for route: gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND jsonPayload.route="/v1/generate"' --limit 50 --project=redwood-prod
- Prometheus quick: curl -s "${PROM}/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(api_responses_total{route='%2Fv1%2Fgenerate',code='429'}[2m]))" | jq .
- Restart single runtime pod: kubectl delete pod ${POD} -n inference --grace-period=30
- Trigger fallback: curl -X POST ${CONTROL_PLANE}/routes/set-fallback -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"model-small-v2","ttl":600}'

Communication templates (short):
- Slack #inc-sre initial post: "IncID: [INC-XXXX] Observed spike in 429s on /v1/generate starting 04:12 UTC. Triage in progress. Mitigations: enabled per-route fallback -> model-small-v2 (TTL 5m). Impact: approx 7% failed requests. Paging: oncall@sre-team."
- Customer-facing blurb (ops): "We're investigating elevated error rates on our generation endpoint; temporary mitigations in place to reduce failures. Will update in 30 minutes."

Post-incident notes (fill as you go):
- Root cause hypothesis: 
- Evidence collected: traces, logs, dumps (attach IDs).
- Actions taken & timestamps: toggles, restarts, rollbacks.
- Follow-ups:
  - Metrics to add to dashboard: per-worker queue depth, avg-token-produce-time
  - Engineering tasks: improved circuit breaker, probe-based autoscale, smarter token caps per route
  - Runbook edits: add automated fallback test in canary pipeline

Known trade-offs / risks:
- Raising rate-limits buys availability at cost of money and possible downstream capacity issues.
- Rolling back may re-expose old bugs.
- Restarting pods may temporarily increase error rate while new pods spin up.

Open TODOs (draft):
- [ ] Add standardized run-level incident tags to traces (route, customer-tier).
- [ ] Implement a quick UI control to test fallback routing without config churn.
- [ ] Add a synthetic streaming-liveness probe to edge proxies.
- [ ] Create a postmortem template that links to economy impact (tokens lost/spend) for each incident.

Notes-to-self (shorthand):
- If you see 429 + low cpu on nodes, check rate-limiter token bucket refill math — we had a bad ceil() bug 2025-08 causing early throttles.
- For streaming stalls: adding a per-connection ping every 10s reduced customer-visible stalls in previous experiment.

Appendix: Useful links & dashboards
- Live SLO dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-inference.com/slo
- Per-route error heatmap: https://dashboards.redwood-inference.com/route-errors
- Control plane toggles: https://console.redwood-inference.com/config/ratelimit
